description: Exploration of a Basic settings view and the existing full settings interface as Advanced. Mock-ups only; example values do not represent live app state.

concepts.notes: A compact set of everyday dictation controls, with short tabs for Dictation, Meetings, and App.
Full settings navigation and the overview dashboard. The current Advanced destination is proposed as Developer options to distinguish it from the view switch.

prompts.basic:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop settings concept for OpenWhisper.
Primary request: Design a new BASIC settings view, as one realistic desktop app screenshot. This is a proposed product design, grounded in the current OpenWhisper settings reference image. Treat the supplied image as a STYLE AND PRODUCT REFERENCE, not an edit target. Make the essentials much easier to find while retaining the identity of the existing product.
Style: faithful to the reference's dark charcoal and midnight navy surfaces, electric blue accent, very subtle borders, small colored outline icons, restrained rounded corners, crisp readable modern sans-serif type. Native desktop utility, flat and practical, no glassmorphism or decorative gradients.
Composition: landscape 1440 by 1080 image with one centered front-facing app window, approximately 1080 by 950, on a plain dark neutral background. Large legible UI text. App window has rounded corners, a minimal title bar, and thin border. No laptop/device/desk. No marketing text outside the window.
Window header: small blue microphone app icon, "OpenWhisper", secondary "Settings". At upper right a clearly visible segmented control "Basic" and "Advanced", with Basic selected blue.
Basic navigation: a short horizontal tab strip below header with exactly "Dictation", "Meetings", "App". Dictation selected. Do not show a large or dense sidebar in this basic view.
Content heading: "Dictation" and helper "The essentials for everyday voice typing."
Main area: a single calm column of three grouped panels, generous breathing room but efficient use of space.
Panel 1 heading "Record"
Row "Microphone" and helper "Used for dictation and meetings." with dropdown "System default".
Row "Recording shortcut" and helper "Press to start or stop dictation." with outlined shortcut pill "Ctrl + Alt + Space" and a small "Change" button.
Panel 2 heading "Transcribe"
Row "Voice model" with selected dropdown "Parakeet" and small quiet status badge "On this computer". Secondary helper "Audio is transcribed locally."
Row "Clean up my dictation" with helper "Fix punctuation and formatting after recording." and a blue ON toggle. Small purple secondary status beneath this row "Cloud provider connected". This row's cleanup text is sent to cloud: do not imply all data stays local.
Panel 3 heading "Output"
Row "Paste text automatically" with helper "Insert the transcript into the active window." and a blue ON toggle.
Row "Show live transcript" with helper "See words appear while you speak." and a gray OFF toggle.
Below panels, unobtrusive link with a right arrow "More dictation options in Advanced".
Footer left a subtle green check with "Changes saved automatically". Footer right one "Done" button.
All text above is verbatim, well-spelled, aligned. Controls must be credible functional UI. No invented logos or badges, no extra settings, no promotional copy, no giant icons. The Basic/Advanced switch is a change of settings view, not a plan or paid tier.
prompts.advanced:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop settings concept for OpenWhisper.
Primary request: Design the matching ADVANCED settings view, as one realistic desktop app screenshot. This is a proposed product design, grounded in the current OpenWhisper settings reference image. Treat the supplied image as a STYLE AND PRODUCT REFERENCE, not an edit target. Preserve the existing depth and grouped navigation, adding a clear reversible Basic/Advanced switch.
Style: faithful to the reference's dark charcoal and midnight navy surfaces, electric blue accent, very subtle borders, small colored outline icons, restrained rounded corners, crisp readable modern sans-serif type. Native desktop utility, flat and practical, no glassmorphism or decorative gradients.
Composition: landscape 1440 by 1080 image with one centered front-facing app window, approximately 1310 by 960, on a plain dark neutral background. Large legible UI text. App window has rounded corners, a minimal title bar, and thin border. No laptop/device/desk. No marketing text outside the window.
Window-wide header: small blue microphone app icon, "OpenWhisper", secondary "Settings". At upper right a clearly visible segmented control "Basic" and "Advanced", with Advanced selected blue. Same visual language as the Basic mock-up.
Below header layout: narrow left rail about 255 pixels and wider content pane.
Rail at top input "Search settings" with small shortcut "Ctrl + K". Selected rail item "Overview" with subtitle "What is running now".
Then compact grouped rail navigation with small outline icons and adequate readable spacing:
group "DICTATION": "Voice model", "Recording", "AI cleanup", "Learned rules", "Profiles", "Remote engine".
group "MEETING MODE": "Voice & speakers", "Intelligence", "Fast judgments", "After the meeting", "Dashboard".
group "MODELS & STORAGE": "Downloads", "Runtime", "Backup".
group "APP": "General", "Hotkeys", "API keys", "MCP", "Developer options".
Developer options is a proposed relabel of the current Advanced page to avoid confusion with the Advanced view switch. Make the rail fit within the window; keep group labels small and items neat, no scrolling clipping.
Content pane heading "Overview" and helper "Your models, workflows, and connections at a glance."
Privacy strip across content, in two adjoining compartments:
green dot "On this computer" and smaller "Dictation audio · Meeting audio · Recordings"
amber dot "Cloud when enabled" and smaller "AI cleanup · Meeting intelligence"
Below, six equally sized dark summary cards in 3 columns and 2 rows with subtle outlines, small icons, and tiny top-right arrows:
card 1 eyebrow "DICTATION", title "Voice model", bold value "Parakeet", detail "On this computer"
card 2 eyebrow "DICTATION", title "AI cleanup", bold value "On", detail "Cloud provider connected"
card 3 eyebrow "DICTATION", title "Cleanup profiles", bold value "2 profiles", detail "Choose a format for each task"
card 4 eyebrow "MEETING MODE", title "Voice & speakers", bold value "Parakeet", detail "English · Speaker labels"
card 5 eyebrow "MEETING MODE", title "Intelligence", bold value "Connected", detail "Cloud provider"
card 6 eyebrow "APP", title "Hotkeys", bold value "Ctrl + Alt + Space", detail "Record dictation"
Next a broad "Models & storage" panel with title "Downloaded speech models", value "4.28 GB", small text "9 of 22 models downloaded", and a slim segmented blue/green/purple/amber storage bar. To its right a narrower "Components" panel with bold "4 of 6 installed" and three brief readiness lines "Speech runtime ready", "GPU acceleration ready", "Meeting agent ready".
A small quiet line beneath cards "API keys: 3 connected · Runtime: Automatic".
Footer left a subtle green check with "Changes saved automatically". Footer right one "Done" button.
All specified UI text verbatim and well-spelled. Keep generous whitespace below the dashboard. No extra settings, promotional text, logos, visual effects, or paid plan implications. Basic and Advanced are views of the same settings, and this advanced view retains access to the complete configuration.
